Vendored static libraries for heif-sys
=======================================

This directory holds prebuilt static libraries and public headers for the HEIF / AVIF decode
stack, so `cargo build` works with no native package manager or build tooling (no vcpkg, cmake,
meson or nasm). The libraries are committed as plain files: cargo's git dependencies don't fetch
Git LFS objects (fire-decode plan, FD16).

Every re-vendor adds a copy of the libraries to every consumer's clone. So re-vendors are
deliberate, not routine, and each target's libraries change in one commit.

Layout: one directory per vendored target
-----------------------------------------
  arm64-macos/     Apple Silicon static libs   (overlay triplet arm64-osx-fire-decode)
  x64-windows/     MSVC x64 static libs, /MT    (overlay triplet x64-windows-fire-decode)
  triplets/        the two overlay triplets

Each target directory holds both `include/` and `lib/` from the same vcpkg run. build.rs picks one
from the target and fails with a named compile_error! on any other target, or on Windows without
the static CRT (FD20).

Contents
--------
One vcpkg baseline for both targets:
  microsoft/vcpkg e529425f2f43d773d0a59517c8d89367d68bb7fd (2026-11-10), vcpkg tool 2026-10-29.

  arm64-macos (built 10 November 2026, Apple clang from Xcode on macOS 27.2):
    lib/libheif.a    libheif  1.23.7   HEIF / AVIF container + API, C++      LGPL-3.0-or-later
    lib/libde265.a   libde265 1.1.3    HEVC decoder, for HEIC / HEIF, C++    LGPL-3.0-or-later
    lib/libdav1d.a   dav1d    1.5.4    AV1 decoder, for AVIF, C              BSD-2-Clause
    include/libheif/ libheif 1.23.7's public headers

  x64-windows (built 11 November 2026, MSVC 19.44.35229 from Visual Studio 2022 on Windows 11):
    lib/heif.lib     libheif  1.23.7   HEIF / AVIF container + API, C++      LGPL-3.0-or-later
    lib/libde265.lib libde265 1.1.3    HEVC decoder, for HEIC / HEIF, C++    LGPL-3.0-or-later
    lib/dav1d.lib    dav1d    1.5.4    AV1 decoder, for AVIF, C              BSD-2-Clause
    include/libheif/ libheif 1.23.7's public headers, identical to arm64-macos's

libheif's and libde265's sources say "version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later
version", so LGPL-3.0-or-later. vcpkg's port metadata says LGPL-3.0-only; the sources decide.

How these were produced
-----------------------
No port patches are needed at this baseline: the libheif port has `dav1d` and `libde265` features,
and for static builds it already compiles dav1d into libheif rather than as a plugin. The overlay
triplet carries the rest:
  - release only;
  - static libraries;
  - macOS 11.0 (VCPKG_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET), which fire, 3D Review and bite all support;
  - Windows /MT (VCPKG_CRT_LINKAGE static), FD20;
  - -DENABLE_PLUGIN_LOADING=OFF for libheif. Plugin loading would be a planted-library risk in a
    COM surrogate or the Quick Look sandbox (FD16).

  git clone https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg && cd vcpkg
  git checkout e529425f2f43d773d0a59517c8d89367d68bb7fd
  ./bootstrap-vcpkg.sh -disableMetrics          (bootstrap-vcpkg.bat on Windows)
  ./vcpkg install "libheif[core,dav1d,libde265]:arm64-osx-fire-decode" \
      --overlay-triplets=<this directory>/triplets --binarysource=clear
  (Windows: "libheif[core,dav1d,libde265]:x64-windows-fire-decode")

`[core,dav1d,libde265]` leaves out the default `hevc` feature, the x265 encoder: no encoders at all.
`--binarysource=clear` builds everything from source. vcpkg fetches the nasm, meson and ninja that
dav1d needs.

Then copy `installed/<triplet>/include/libheif` and the three libraries from
`installed/<triplet>/lib` into the target's directory here.

Checks after each re-vendor (all passed for arm64-macos on 10 November 2026, and for x64-windows
on 11 November 2026)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  libheif references its codecs:  nm -u lib/libheif.a | grep -c dav1d      (> 0; 10 here)
                                  nm -u lib/libheif.a | grep -c de265      (> 0; 26 here)
  no plugin loading:              nm -u lib/libheif.a | grep -c dlopen     (0)
                                  strings lib/libheif.a | grep -c LIBHEIF_PLUGIN_PATH   (0)
                                  (Windows: no LoadLibrary import from libheif)
  no encoders:                    nm lib/libheif.a | grep -c -i x265_      (0)
  macOS deployment target:        otool -l lib/*.a | grep -A4 LC_BUILD_VERSION | grep minos
                                                                             (11.0 for all three)
  Windows CRT:                    the libraries carry /DEFAULTLIB:LIBCMT, not MSVCRT
  gain-map API (FD17):            grep -i -E "gain.?map|tmap|21496" include/libheif/*.h
                                                                             (none in 1.23.7)

  On Windows, from Git Bash with LLVM and the MSVC tools on PATH (no `strings` there):
    llvm-nm -u lib/heif.lib | grep -c dav1d                          (10)
    llvm-nm -u lib/heif.lib | grep -c de265                          (26)
    llvm-nm -u lib/<each>.lib | grep -c -i -E "LoadLibrary|dlopen"   (0 for all three)
    grep -a -c LIBHEIF_PLUGIN_PATH lib/<each>.lib                    (0 for all three)
    llvm-nm lib/<each>.lib | grep -c -i -E "x265_|aom_codec_enc|rav1e_|svt_av1_enc|kvz_"
                                                                     (0 for all three)
    dumpbin -directives lib/<each>.lib | grep -i -o "/DEFAULTLIB:[^ ]*" | sort | uniq -c
                    (LIBCMT, LIBCPMT, OLDNAMES, uuid only; no MSVCRT / MSVCPRT)
  heif.lib still names heif_load_plugin(s): the API stays, and returns "not supported" when built
  without plugin loading.

  Then the crate's whole suite with every feature, against these libraries:
    RUSTFLAGS="-C target-feature=+crt-static" \
        cargo test -p fire-decode --features psd,heif,icc,raw,mips   (253 passed, as on macOS)

Stripping (Windows only)
------------------------
vcpkg's release build on MSVC embeds CodeView debug info (/Z7) in the .obj files, which balloons
heif.lib to ~219 MB (libde265.lib ~20 MB, dav1d.lib ~8 MB). Remove it with llvm-objcopy; code,
symbols and /DEFAULTLIB directives stay, leaving 52.9, 3.4 and 3.8 MB:

       llvm-objcopy --strip-debug heif.lib
       llvm-objcopy --strip-debug dav1d.lib
       llvm-objcopy --strip-debug libde265.lib

The arm64-macos release build carries no such debug info; those .a files are ~6.4 MB as produced.

Linking
-------
Windows: the MSVC objects embed /DEFAULTLIB directives for the C++ runtime libheif and libde265
need, so it links itself and build.rs must not name it.
macOS: Mach-O has no equivalent, so build.rs names `c++` explicitly, or libheif's and libde265's
C++ symbols go unresolved.

History
-------
fire vendored an earlier build of this stack under its own crates/heif-sys/vendor (libheif 1.23.0
on Windows, 1.23.2 on macOS, built for macOS 27.0). Those binaries stay in fire's history for its past releases'
notices; this repository's history was rewritten without them, and starts from this re-vendor.
